clue.text: Determined to have an enjoyable time with a crook?

definitions.text: Determined to have an enjoyable time with a crook?

parts.words: Determined to have an enjoyable time with a crook?
parts.note: an idiom for being set on having fun, with the question mark pointing to bent as a crook as well as inclined

explanation.surface: Someone eager for a good time in the company of a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' in the phrase means set on or inclined; the clue teases its slang sense of crooked, a crook being bent in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone resolutely seeking fun or enjoyment.

clue.text: Remedy for one spotted in ta taking a nap strangely

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take in the other piece, holding it inside them
done strangely, the letters of a nap are rearranged

parts.note: an ace is the card or die face with a single spot

explanation.surface: A cure for a spotty person found by having a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns A NAP into PANA, and 'taking' puts ACE inside it, after PAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed cure-all, a universal remedy.

clue.text: Quits the flat

explanation.surface: Settling up over an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quits means owing nothing either way, square; a flat surface is level, with no bumps.

clue.text: Imagined having had some food, so upset inside

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, as the clue says

parts.note: to sup is to eat an evening meal

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the little word is turned upside down, read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone thought they had eaten and felt queasy inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SO into OS, which goes 'inside' SUPPED.
explanation.definitionFit: Supposed and imagined both mean assumed or believed without proof.

clue.text: Offhurried the detectives

parts.note: hurried means ran
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch

explanation.surface: The police detectives rushed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is off has gone bad, smelling sour and stale.

clue.text: Beautiful Italian woman finds a poisonous plant

explanation.surface: A lovely Italian lady discovers deadly nightshade.
explanation.definitionFit: In Italian the phrase means a lovely lady; it is also the name of deadly nightshade, a toxic herb.

clue.text: Getting closer, could be in range

indicators.note: says the letters could be arranged into another word

explanation.surface: Something approaching might be within reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Approaching or coming near something is drawing closer.

clue.text: Bent on submission

parts.note: describes kneeling in surrender, rather than being determined to submit something

explanation.definitionFit: Kneeling, posture bent low, is the classic gesture of surrender or begging.

clue.text: Support below peg

parts.note: below means under
a peg is a pin

explanation.surface: A support placed beneath a peg.
explanation.definitionFit: To underpin is to support from beneath, like foundations.

clue.text: Get to know slim redhead who has been included

indicators.note: the head letter has been taken into the other word, sitting inside it

parts.note: slim means lean
the head, first letter, of red is R

explanation.surface: Meeting a slender ginger-haired person who joined the group.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn something is to come to know it.

clue.text: Lucky one, she went round the plant

indicators.note: letters going round in circles are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A fortunate woman walked around the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeysuckle is a climbing shrub, woodbine, with fragrant flowers.

clue.text: Not repeated in the past

explanation.surface: A one-off from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: It means a single time only, and also formerly, at some earlier time.

clue.text: Authority of monk over one country

parts.note: Dom is a title given to a Benedictine monk
I is the Roman numeral for one
a country is a nation

explanation.surface: A monk's power over a whole country.
explanation.definitionFit: Domination is control or power over others, ruling authority.

clue.text: This nun I'd found struggling with a foreign language

indicators.note: the letters struggle and tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A nun finds a foreign tongue hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges THIS NUN I'D together with the A from 'with a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindustani is a language of northern India, the basis of Hindi and Urdu.

clue.text: Once a pitman, now an inspector

parts.note: ex- means formerly, once
a pitman works down a coal pit, a miner

explanation.surface: A former coal miner now works as an inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: An examiner inspects or tests things, as an official checker.

clue.text: Father shortly goes round the workshops

indicators.note: going round signals the letters being turned about into a new order

parts.note: FR is the short form of Father, as a priest's title

explanation.surface: A dad briefly tours the workshops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' mixes FR with GOES to give FORGES.
explanation.definitionFit: A forge is a smithy, a blacksmith's workshop.

clue.text: A party getting in the money for a tropical tree

indicators.note: the pieces get inside the other word

parts.note: money is cash
Lab is short for Labour, the UK political party

explanation.surface: A political party gets hold of funds for a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting in' puts A and LAB inside CASH, after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: The calabash is a tropical American tree bearing gourd-like fruit.

clue.text: Withdraw this in France-Dee's upset about

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece sits around the other
upset here means the letters are knocked over and shuffled into a new order

parts.note: the name Dee with its S
ce is French for this

explanation.surface: Dee is unhappy about leaving a French group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges DEES into SEDE, which goes 'about' CE, after its SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To secede is to withdraw formally from a union or alliance.

clue.text: Plays around in company during the folk-song

indicators.note: the jumbled word is placed in the other piece
letters moved around fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A troupe performs a traditional song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns PLAYS into ALYPS, which goes 'in' CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a Caribbean ballad, a West Indian folk-style song.

clue.text: Keep mother in anti-movement

parts.note: Ma is a familiar word for mother
taken as written

indicators.note: movement of the letters puts them into a new order

explanation.surface: Mother stays in a protest group.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain something is to keep or preserve it.

clue.text: It's agony not starting to lose one's strength!

indicators.note: not starting means losing the first letter

parts.note: to languish is to grow weak or feeble

explanation.surface: Losing your strength is painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' drops the L from LANGUISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguish is severe mental or physical suffering, torment.

clue.text: Regard movement of road-building machine

indicators.note: movement of the letters puts them into a new order

explanation.surface: Considering how a roadworks vehicle moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A grader is a bulldozer-like vehicle that levels surfaces for roads.

clue.text: Not a burn on the Scottish border?

definitions.text: Not a burn on the Scottish border?

parts.words: Not a burn on the Scottish border?
parts.note: a burn is a Scottish stream, but also a scald; the opposite of a hot thing is chilly water, and the clue points to a border town

explanation.surface: Asking about something that is not a scald near Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Coldstream is a town on the River Tweed, on the border between Scotland and England.
explanation.definitionFit: The town's name splits into words for chilly water, the opposite of something hot.

clue.text: Big fellow so backward

indicators.note: backward says the word is read from end to start

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, so

explanation.surface: A large man is so backward.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a fairy-tale giant, a huge brute.

clue.text: Leading sea-power

explanation.surface: A top naval nation.
explanation.definitionFit: It means chief or principal, the open ocean in poetry, and force as in might and main.

clue.text: New plate contained some Greek coins

indicators.note: something new is a fresh version, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh plate held some ancient coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepta are small Greek coins, a hundredth of a drachma.

clue.text: Striking on stage

explanation.surface: An impressive theatre performance.
explanation.definitionFit: It means arresting or vivid, and also relating to plays and theatre.

clue.text: Comparatively sanctimonious

parts.note: a phrase built on a comparative adjective, meaning smugly pious compared with someone else

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a self-righteous person who feels morally better than others.
